note: Read from the vendored file at the digest above, the whole 607,055 bytes. Elements are grouped by the design's regions in template order: titlebar, drawer, fleet, audit, settings, thread notices, launcher, conversation, composer, dock, handoff, fullscreen preview, palette. `where` and `states` are for the human reading the design; the gate holds copy and evidence only. Sample data is the fictional session (acme-api, the Stripe webhook task, mac-mini-m4 and friends) and is claimed under `sample` with no element. Re-derived 2026-09-23 after the audit design prompts: I69 (archive), J10 (build line), J18 (API keys), J23 (pairing card, imported from PairingCard and inventoried in pairing-card-v2.json), J24 and J37 (login service), J25 (TailnetReach, tailnet-reach-v2.json), J27 (commits and pull request), J32 (running apps), J34 (checkpoint before a write), J39 (search every machine), J40 (RemoteBrowser, remote-browser-v2.json), J42 (images per model), J43 (adopted sessions), J45 (tool calls, see skills-v2.json). Much of the new copy lives in the design's data (menus, notices, launcher chips); the elements name it in `where`.

handleWebhook runs its side effects before the event is recorded, so any Stripe retry replays them. Two duplicate invoice emails and one double charge in the last 30 days trace to this.

Claim the event id in its own transaction, then do the work, then commit the claim. A retry that arrives before the first attempt finishes loses the claim race and returns early instead of running twice.
New table webhook_replay with event_id as the primary key, a claimed_at column and a committed_at column. The unique constraint is what makes the claim atomic, not application code.

A crash between claim and commit leaves a claim with no committed_at. Step 1 adds a 15 minute expiry so those events are retried rather than lost forever, and step 4 covers it with a test.
Handlers that are not idempotent internally are still not idempotent. This makes delivery exactly-once, it does not make a half-finished handler safe to resume.
The migration is additive and takes no locks on existing tables, so it is safe to run on production later. This plan does not run it there.
